result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives a full, compact type scale from the name down to the footer, with four or five levels, tracked small caps for section labels and clear spacing that puts more room between sections than between items. It also sets every price to two decimals and aligns them on a right tab stop, all in one font family. B covers most of the rubric and adds a useful sample layout, but it brings in more styling (several suggested fonts, rules, ornaments, italic plus grey), and its '£4.50 each' entry breaks the common right edge. A has small slips: it suggests a non-breaking space before the percent sign, and it overstates how right alignment handles proportional figures. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give full point sizes, consistent two-decimal prices on a right tab, and more space between sections than between items. B is tighter: it uses about four size levels in a single family, says outright not to justify, and gives clear steps for setting up paragraph styles. A also does well and includes a worked mock-up, but it lists several typeface options and adds rules and ornaments. B has two small flaws: its claim that dot leaders are what make a menu look like a spreadsheet is dubious, and its advice to put a space before the % sign is odd.
